editorial:
Set in early 1700s England, this dark comedy follows Queen Anne, a frail and lonely ruler who leans heavily on her close friend Sarah Churchill. When Sarah's cousin Abigail arrives at court looking for a job, she quickly charms her way into the Queen's good graces. What starts as a simple rivalry between two cousins soon turns into a full-blown power struggle, with both women fighting for control over the Queen and the kingdom. The movie is sharp, funny, and surprisingly mean in the best way, with witty dialogue and wild camera work that keeps you on your toes.

The acting is the real star here. Olivia Colman is brilliant as the unpredictable Queen, while Rachel Weisz and Emma Stone bring fire and charm to their roles. The pacing is quick and the humor is dry, so if you enjoy clever, character-driven stories with a dark edge, you will have a great time. The only downside is that some scenes feel a bit strange and may not be for everyone. endingExplained: In the final scenes, Abigail wins the battle and becomes the Queen's favourite, while Sarah is banished from court. But the victory feels hollow. The Queen, now fully dependent on Abigail, forces her to rub her legs while she watches rabbits, a reminder of her lost children. Abigail looks trapped and miserable, realizing she has become a servant rather than a true friend. The movie ends with the Queen's power over both women, showing that winning the Queen's favor comes at a heavy personal cost.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves sharp dialogue, strong female leads, and dark humor.
